title: Ride the cable car to the Big Buddha at Ngong Ping
description: The 5.7km cabin ride climbs over the airport before Lantau's hills; pay extra for a glass-bottomed Crystal Cabin. The 268 steps up to the seated bronze Buddha are free, the monastery vegetarian lunch is not.

title: Wander the stilt houses of Tai O fishing village
description: Small boats putter out from the jetty hoping to spot the rare pink dolphins that live in the estuary, though sightings are getting rarer every year. Go for the dried shrimp paste and the houses built on stilts over the water, not just the dolphins.

title: Eat claypot rice at Temple Street Night Market
description: Stalls don't open properly until after dark, so arrive after 7pm. Fortune tellers cluster at the southern end and street opera singers turn up unannounced most nights.

title: Climb past golden statues to the Ten Thousand Buddhas Monastery
description: Around 430 steps lined with life-sized golden arhat statues, each with a different face, lead up from Sha Tin station. There are actually closer to 13,000 Buddha statues inside, not ten thousand.

title: Breathe incense smoke under the coils at Man Mo Temple
description: Built in 1847 on Hollywood Road for the gods of literature and war, hung with spiral incense coils that smoulder for weeks. Come mid-morning before the tour groups arrive off the escalator.

title: Take a sampan through Aberdeen's floating harbour
description: Boat people have lived on the water here for generations, and a handful of sampan operators still run short putters through the anchored junks and floating seafood stalls. Agree the price before you step aboard, it is not metered.

title: Pick your own dinner from the tanks in Sai Kung
description: Hong Kong's 'back garden' — a waterfront town where restaurants keep live grouper and mantis shrimp in tanks by the door, and boats leave for the hexagonal rock columns of the Global Geopark. Go out on the water first, eat after.

title: Taste free almond cookie samples on Senado Square
description: The wave-patterned Portuguese pavement leads past bakeries handing out free samples of almond cookies and beef jerky, which is why nobody ever finishes just one shop. Weekday mornings beat the weekend crush.

title: Bungee jump off the Macau Tower
description: At 233 metres this was once the world's highest commercial bungee jump. If you'd rather keep your feet under you, the SkyWalk lets you circle the outer rim of the tower on nothing but a harness.

title: Visit the temple that gave Macau its name
description: Built before the Portuguese arrived, this is reputedly where sailors asked locals the name of the place and were told 'A-Ma-Gao' — Bay of A-Ma — which became Macau. The incense smoke inside is thick enough to sting the eyes.

title: Ride an indoor gondola through the Venetian's canals
description: A painted sky ceiling and a singing gondolier inside the world's largest casino floor, a short walk from three more resort casinos on the Cotai Strip. Book the gondola slot online, the weekend walk-up queue runs over an hour.

title: Watch sunset turn the Flaming Cliffs orange at Bayanzag
description: An American Museum of Natural History expedition found the first dinosaur eggs ever identified here in 1923. The red sandstone only lights up properly in the last hour before dark, so time the visit for late afternoon.

title: Watch wrestling, archery and horse racing at Naadam
description: The national stadium hosts the opening ceremony and wrestling on 11-12 July, but the horse races happen out on the open steppe well outside town and are free to watch if you can find transport there.

title: Ride a horse along the shore of Khövsgöl Lake
description: Mongolians call it the Mother Sea. It holds close to a third of Central Asia's fresh water and stays clear enough to see boulders metres down. Reindeer-herding Tsaatan families camp near the north end in summer.

title: Walk the 108 stupas ringing Erdene Zuu Monastery
description: Built in 1585 from the stones of Karakorum, Genghis Khan's ruined capital next door, using rubble nobody else wanted. Count the stupas on the outer wall if the monks let you in before the tour buses.

title: Climb Turtle Rock in Gorkhi-Terelj National Park
description: A granite boulder shaped uncannily like a turtle, an easy two-hour round trip from the park entrance and the most-photographed rock formation in Mongolia. Stay overnight in a ger camp rather than day-tripping from Ulaanbaatar, the park empties out after the buses leave.

title: Spot wild takhi horses in Khustain Nuruu
description: Przewalski's horses, the only truly wild horse species left, went extinct here in the 1960s and were reintroduced from zoo-bred stock in the 1990s. Dawn and dusk drives give the best odds of seeing a herd.

title: Walk the ice gorge of Yolyn Am in the middle of the Gobi
description: A narrow limestone canyon so shaded that ice can survive on the floor into July, a strange thing to find inside a desert park. The gorge narrows to a couple of metres wide near the end, so go early before the wind picks up.

title: Drive onto the frozen lake at the Khövsgöl Ice Festival
description: By early March the lake ice is thick enough for trucks, and Khatgal hosts ice wrestling, horse-drawn sled races and a very cold cousin of sumo out on the frozen surface. Nights drop below minus thirty, dress like you mean it.

title: Take a boat across the turquoise water of Attabad Lake
description: A 2010 landslide dammed the Hunza River and drowned a stretch of the Karakoram Highway under water this shade of blue. Speedboats now cross where the old road used to run, past the submerged tops of buildings in low-water years.

title: Cross into China at the Khunjerab Pass
description: At 4,693 metres this is the highest paved border crossing on earth, and the drive up from Sost through Khunjerab National Park is as much the point as the border marker itself. It closes with the first heavy snow, usually by December.

title: Trek to K2 Base Camp through the Karakoram
description: Roughly two weeks on foot from Askole to Concordia, where four of the world's fourteen eight-thousand-metre peaks stand around you at once. Porters and permits need arranging in Skardu well ahead, this is not a walk-up trek.

title: Camp on the high plateau of Deosai National Park
description: Locals call it the Land of Giants: one of the highest plateaus on earth, carpeted in wildflowers for a few weeks each summer and home to the Himalayan brown bear. Snow closes the only access road from October to May.

title: Cross the Hussaini suspension bridge below the Passu Cones
description: Missing planks and a serious sway make this one of the more nerve-testing footbridges anyone crosses on purpose, strung over the Hunza River under a ridge of jagged rock spires. Go early morning for the light on the cones and a bridge to yourself.

title: Watch the call to prayer echo across Badshahi Mosque's courtyard
description: Built in 1673 by Aurangzeb, the courtyard alone holds around a hundred thousand worshippers and still fills for Friday prayers. Climb one of the minarets, when it's open, for a view straight down into the fort across the square.

title: See the flag lowering ceremony at the Wagah border
description: Pakistan Rangers and India's Border Security Force high-kick through a choreographed rivalry every evening before sunset, with grandstands packed on both sides of the gate. Arrive at least an hour early on weekends or you'll be watching from the back.

title: Eat under the fort walls on Lahore's Food Street
description: Restaurant rooftops along this pedestrianised strip face the floodlit Badshahi Mosque and fort walls, which makes it worth the markup tourists get charged over the food halls elsewhere in the old city.

title: Walk the streets of the 4,500-year-old city of Mohenjo-daro
description: One of the best-preserved cities of the Indus Valley Civilisation, laid out on a grid with covered drains centuries before Rome existed. Go in winter — Sindh's summer heat on the exposed brick site is brutal by mid-morning.

title: Stand beneath Faisal Mosque's tent-shaped roof
description: Pakistan's largest mosque skips the usual dome for a Bedouin-tent silhouette by a Turkish architect, set against the Margalla Hills. It can hold over a hundred thousand people and still feels empty on a weekday morning.

title: Drive the green switchbacks of the Swat Valley
description: Called Pakistan's Switzerland for its pine forests and river valleys, and once the heart of the Buddhist Gandhara civilisation — ruined stupas still sit above the orchards. Check the current security situation before planning a route beyond Mingora.

title: Ride a wooden launch on the Buriganga through Old Dhaka
description: Sadarghat terminal moves more river traffic than almost anywhere on earth — hire a small wooden boat for twenty minutes and watch the chaos from the water instead of the ghat. The colour and the smell both hit hardest before 9am.

title: Count the pillars inside the Sixty Dome Mosque
description: Built in the 1450s by a Turkish general, it actually has seventy-seven domes; the name comes from the sixty stone pillars holding the roof up, not a mistranslation anyone bothered to fix. Bagerhat is a long side trip from Khulna, not a Dhaka day trip.

title: Explore the unfinished Mughal fort of Lalbagh
description: Started in 1678 and never finished after the governor's daughter died here and the project was abandoned as ill-omened. Her tomb, the Pari Bibi mausoleum, is still the best-preserved building on site.

title: Climb the pyramid-shaped ruins of Paharpur monastery
description: The largest Buddhist monastery south of the Himalayas, an eighth-century complex that housed thousands of monks and now looks like a stepped brick pyramid from a distance. It's a full day's travel from Dhaka, so pair it with Bogura or stay overnight in Naogaon.

title: Snorkel the coral reef off Saint Martin's Island
description: Bangladesh's only coral island, three hours by boat from Teknaf and closed to boat traffic outside the winter season. The reef is thin compared to its neighbours but the coconut-lined beaches and the sea turtle nesting sites are the real draw.

title: Paddle through the flooded trees of Ratargul Swamp Forest
description: One of very few freshwater swamp forests left anywhere, nicknamed the Amazon of Bangladesh, only fully navigable by boat when the monsoon floods the forest floor. Come dry season and you'll mostly be looking at tree trunks in mud.
